item.title: China’s Open-Weight Challenge to U.S. AI Leadership
item.description: The United States hedged it bets on AI leadership driven by frontier models. This bet could be losing ground to a cheaper, open alternative.

item.title: Iran and the Emerging Security Order in the Middle East
item.description: The war with Iran has reshaped the Middle East, exposing the limits of U.S. power and raising questions about the future of regional security. As the old order unravels, Tehran may emerge with greater influence in a more multipolar region.

item.title: AUKUS Turns Five: Real Progress, Hard Challenges Ahead
item.description: Five years on, the AUKUS partnership has built the scaffolding for deterrence. Now it has to prove the scaffolding can bear weight.

item.title: A Pacific Leaders Meeting with Too Few Leaders
item.description: As Pacific leaders gathered to strengthen regional unity, intensifying geopolitical competition put the region’s growing strategic importance—and its autonomy—squarely in the spotlight.

item.title: How Do the Latest Black Sea Attacks Affect Global Food Security?
item.description: For the first time since 2022, attacks on agricultural infrastructure and cargo vessels are limiting grain exports from Russia and Ukraine at the same time. CSIS experts examine the latest attacks, their food-security impacts, and how the Iran war is worsening the crisis.

item.title: Hormuz Needs a Community, Not a Condominium
item.description: A deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz that sidelines Gulf states would entrench coercion and invite a new conflict. Postwar Europe offers a better model: a shared governance mechanism that dilutes leverage and fosters long-term cooperation.

item.title: The Billion-Dollar Chip: Who Can Afford to Design the Future?
item.description: As the cost of designing leading-edge chips approaches $1 billion, frontier semiconductor design is becoming accessible to fewer firms. The United States must reduce the underlying cost of design to preserve innovation and competitiveness across critical industries.

item.title: Imagining an Insurgency in Post-Revolutionary Iran
item.description: What if the United States invades Iran to restore regional stability? Iran’s post-regime military strategy would rely on insurgent warfare to draw the United States into a protracted conflict, impeding U.S. efforts to achieve long-term political goals.

item.title: Does Vietnam’s Soaring U.S. Trade Deficit Make It a Bad Actor?
item.description: There is little if any justification for any trade policy crackdown on Vietnam for allegedly being a bad actor, harming U.S. economic interests, or aiding and abetting China’s trade interests.

item.title: Adapting to the New Terrorism Landscape 25 Years After 9/11
item.description: Post-9/11 counterterrorism efforts made large, foreign-directed attacks harder to execute. Stopping the terrorist threat that remains today requires a new approach.
